## Building the future of voice teaching

In 2024, I started building something that didn't exist: an AI-powered system that helps voice teachers teach better.

Not a replacement for the teacher. A tool that extends what's possible in the studio.

## What the system does

- **Lesson analysis**: Transcribes voice lessons and generates pedagogical analysis — identifying teaching patterns, student responses, and moments of progress
- **Pre-lesson briefs**: Pulls from a student's full history (past lessons, reflections, repertoire, acoustic data) to prepare the teacher before each session
- **Practice plans**: Generates individualized practice plans based on what happened in the lesson
- **Student portal**: A web-based dashboard where students can view their progress, reflections, and plans

## How it's built

Python, Claude API (Anthropic), Supabase (database + authentication), Obsidian sync, and Quarto publishing. The system is grounded in a complete pedagogical framework — co-investigation model, motor learning phases, exercise taxonomy, and safety protocols — all encoded in the AI's operating instructions.

## Why this matters

Voice teaching has been a one-to-one, ephemeral practice for centuries. What happens in the lesson stays in the lesson — unless the student remembers it. This system creates a persistent, analyzable record of the teaching and learning process. It makes the invisible visible.

I believe this kind of tool will reshape voice pedagogy in the next decade. And I want to make sure it's built by people who actually understand voices — not just algorithms.
